title: Birth plans, newborn weeks and the sick child

say: Birth plans, the newborn weeks, and the sick child.
This is the video for module 2 of Maternal and Child Health Literacy.
Labour often starts at night, or when the person you rely on is away. Families who decide in advance save precious time.

say: Most newborn deaths happen in the first week, so the checks after birth matter.

say: A birth and emergency plan answers five questions. Where will the baby be born, and which bigger hospital for an emergency? WHO says all births should have a skilled attendant.

panel.heading: Five parts, written on one page
items: Card and bag by the door from week 36

say: Who goes with the mother, and who can decide to leave if her husband is away?

panel.heading: Five parts, written on one page
items: Card and bag by the door from week 36

say: Who will drive, day and night? Save two numbers, and a second option.

panel.heading: Five parts, written on one page
items: Card and bag by the door from week 36

say: How much will it cost? Ask the facility, not the market.

panel.heading: Five parts, written on one page
items: Card and bag by the door from week 36

say: And keep the card and the bag by the door from week 36. Plan for at least 24 hours in the facility after birth. Share the plan with two people.

panel.heading: Five parts, written on one page
items: Card and bag by the door from week 36

say: Zainab is 16 weeks pregnant. A night trip to the general hospital costs about 7,500 naira one way. Prices vary by town and time.
Two trips come to 15,000 naira, and she adds about 10,000 for other costs.
That is 25,000 naira. She has 20 weeks until week 36, so 25,000 divided by 20 is 1,250 naira a week.
She keeps it in a separate mobile money wallet, and her sister knows how to reach it.
Babies lose heat very quickly. Dry the baby and place them skin-to-skin on the mother's chest, covered with a cloth.

panel.heading: Essential newborn care
items: Only breast milk for six months
Nothing on the cord: keep it clean, dry

say: Start breastfeeding within one hour of birth. The thick yellowish first milk is good for the baby.

panel.heading: Essential newborn care
items: Only breast milk for six months
Nothing on the cord: keep it clean, dry

say: Give only breast milk for the first six months. No water, no glucose water, no herbal drinks.

panel.heading: Essential newborn care
items: Only breast milk for six months
Nothing on the cord: keep it clean, dry

say: Keep the cord stump clean and dry. Ash, oil or any home mixture can bring infection.

panel.heading: Essential newborn care
items: Only breast milk for six months
Nothing on the cord: keep it clean, dry

say: WHO recommends at least 24 hours in the facility after birth, then three more checks in six weeks. For example, Chioma gave birth on Tuesday 14 July.

panel.heading: Postnatal checks in six weeks
items: At least 24 hours in the facility

say: Her first check is due 16 or 17 July.

panel.heading: Postnatal checks in six weeks
items: At least 24 hours in the facility

say: The next is between 21 and 28 July.

panel.heading: Postnatal checks in six weeks
items: At least 24 hours in the facility

say: And the week six check is due around 25 August. They write the dates on the baby's card and in both phones.

panel.heading: Postnatal checks in six weeks
items: At least 24 hours in the facility
panel.rule: If the clinic gives different dates, follow the clinic.

say: A newborn with any of these signs goes to a facility today. Do not wait for the next check.
Keep the baby warm against the mother's skin, keep offering the breast, and bring the card. No herbal mixtures, glucose water or medicines on the way.
And watch the mother too. Heavy bleeding, fever, severe headache or fits mean go now.

panel.heading: Newborn danger signs
items: Not feeding well, or stopped feeding
Very sleepy, floppy, or not moving
Fever, or the baby feels cold

say: Check for go-now signs first, every time. Cannot drink or breastfeed, fits, very sleepy or floppy, or breathing fast with the chest pulling in. Any one of these means go to a facility now.

panel.heading: Home care with a health worker, or go now?
left: Fast breathing or chest pulling in
right: Keep notes on stools and fever

say: If there are none, care at home while you see a health worker. Keep breastfeeding more often, and write down the stools, fevers and drinks.

panel.heading: Home care with a health worker, or go now?
left: Fast breathing or chest pulling in
right: Keep notes on stools and fever

say: Diarrhoea is 3 or more loose or watery stools in a day. The danger is dehydration. Mix ORS, oral rehydration solution, exactly as the packet says, with clean water, and ask the health worker how much to give.
Sunken eyes or restlessness mean go to a health worker. Very sleepy or unable to drink means go now.

cards.d: 3 or more loose stools a day. Mix ORS exactly as the packet says; ask the health worker how much.
Get a malaria test before treatment. Many fevers are not malaria.
Fast breathing or chest pulling in: go now. Medicines come from a health worker.

say: For fever, WHO recommends a malaria test before treatment. Never give leftover medicine from another child.

cards.d: 3 or more loose stools a day. Mix ORS exactly as the packet says; ask the health worker how much.
Get a malaria test before treatment. Many fevers are not malaria.
Fast breathing or chest pulling in: go now. Medicines come from a health worker.

say: For cough with fast breathing or the lower chest sucking in, go now. Antibiotics are chosen by a health worker.

cards.d: 3 or more loose stools a day. Mix ORS exactly as the packet says; ask the health worker how much.
Get a malaria test before treatment. Many fevers are not malaria.
Fast breathing or chest pulling in: go now. Medicines come from a health worker.

say: To remember. Write the plan and save weekly. Keep the newborn warm and breastfed, with nothing on the cord. Keep the postnatal dates. Any danger sign means go to a facility now. And medicines only from a health worker.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Breastfeed within one hour; nothing on the cord
Three postnatal checks in six weeks
Newborn or child danger sign: go now
Test for malaria; no medicines without a health worker

say: Your turn. Write a one-page birth plan with your saving target, make a postnatal date card with the newborn danger signs, and prepare a sick-child kit with ORS and a go-now card.
